proposals.hypothesis: LiF is a very wide-gap, electronically insulating fluoride with F- in its most stable anion state and an extremely negative formation energy. It should resist oxidation at 4 V vs Li/Li+ on the LCO side. Its only cation is Li+, so it cannot exchange La or Zr with LLZO, which is the source of the penalties seen for Li3PO4, LiAlO2, Li2ZrO3 and Li3BO3. A fluoride family has not been tested yet, so this explores a new chemistry.
proposals.motivation: Earlier oxide and phosphate/borate coatings (Li3PO4 0.099, LiAlO2 0.083, Li2ZrO3 0.300, Li3BO3 0.313 eV/non-Li atom) were all penalized by LLZO contact reactions that released La- or Zr-containing products. A fluoride with Li-only cations is expected to avoid those displacement reactions.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating phosphate that is widely used as a cathode coating. Its P-O network is oxidatively stable near 4 V vs Li, and it is chemically compatible with both LiCoO2 and the garnet LLZO, so it should give a low interfacial penalty while meeting the band-gap and insulation requirements.

LiAlO2 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating oxide with Al3+ in a highly stable oxidation state. It resists oxidation near 4 V vs Li/Li+ and is thermodynamically compatible with the Li-rich garnet LLZO, since Al3+ does not readily reduce or displace La/Zr. Its contact reaction energy with LLZO should be lower than the 0.099 eV/atom found for Li3PO4, which reacted to LaPO4, ZrO2 and O2. It is also a standard LCO coating material, so it should give a low interfacial penalty.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 showed a contact penalty of 0.099 eV/non-Li atom (bin 4, not acceptable) from LLZO-driven decomposition to LaPO4/ZrO2/O2. A different, more inert oxide family is needed to reduce that penalty.
